title: Prepare a wet microscope mount
context: Wet-mount preparation is a common manual sample-preparation step in research microscopy. The physical outcome is a released coverslip with a continuous liquid film over the specimen, without a large trapped air pocket; this task stops before microscope imaging.
setup: One75×25×1mm glass slide on an80×30×29mm support; one loose22×22×0.15mm glass coverslip on a10×10×36.5mm pickup pedestal; a6×6mm nonliving optical specimen and10µL dyed water centred on the slide. Slide centre(330,25,777)mm; coverslip centre(330,-65,784.075)mm. Original YAM station.
scoring: After1s released, supported and still, with the cover entirely on the slide:1.0 if at least98% of the central12×12mm region is wet and no trapped-air component exceeds the area of a1mm-diameter circle;0.5 if at least50% is wet;otherwise0. Interarm collision gives0. Final state, not peak score.
fidelity: Native rigid glass/contact/gravity at960Hz; original20Hz controls. A conservative10µL grid approximates squeezing and air sealing from the live cover plane, with a20µm regularized film gap. Coloured tracer visualizes this material state. No calibrated CFD, capillary reaction force, refractive optics or glass fracture. The cover is never attached or relocated by code.
instruction: Prepare a wet mount on the microscope slide using the loose coverslip. Cover the central specimen region with a continuous liquid film, leaving no large trapped air pocket. Leave the coverslip fully supported and released on the slide. Any successful grasp or placement strategy is allowed.
scores: Dream-1: 0.0/2400 actions/120 s; scripted demo: 1.0/1000 actions/50 s
reset_notes: Fresh fixed reset, original calibrated station. Replace or clean consumed material and restore the documented finite preload before every real trial.
